newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Nuclear reactor survey team to visit North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear reactor survey team to visit North Korea.

text.p: A multinational consortium supervising the construction of nuclear reactors in North Korea will send a 30-member survey team to the North late next week, a South Korean Foreign Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The seventh site survey team will be deployed to North Korea on February 22," he told Reuters. "The surveyors would stay for a maximum of five months."

The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO), led by South Korea, Japan and the United States, supervises the building of light-water reactors in Shinpo, North Korea, in return for the communist state freezing its suspected nuclear weapons programme.
The move to send the team was among steps to ease tensions on the Korean peninsular after last September's incursion into southern waters of a North Korean submarine, which landed 26 armed agents.
The incursion froze all contacts between the two Koreas, which remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce, not in a peace agreement.
North Korea issued a rare official apology in December over the incursion and Seoul responded in January by reopening the door for investment by local companies in the North.
Last month KEDO signed protocols with North Korea for building the reactors, which put a 1994 agreement between Washington and Pyongyang back on track.
Under the agreement signed in Geneva in October 1994, North Korea promised to dismantle its weapons-grade nuclear programme in return for safer light-water reactors.
